The first Olympic Games are recorded in Greece.
Traditional date of the founding of Rome.
The Athenians defeat the Persians at Marathon.
The Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta begins.
Socrates is condemned to death in Athens.
Alexander the Great dies in Babylon; his generals divide his empire.
Ashoka becomes emperor of the Maurya Empire in India (c. 268) and later embraces Buddhism.
The Qin unify China; Shi Huangdi becomes the first emperor.
The Han dynasty is founded in China.
Julius Caesar is assassinated in Rome.
Augustus becomes the first Roman emperor.
Wang Mang seizes the Han throne in China (Xin dynasty, 9–23).
The Roman invasion of Britain begins.
Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii and Herculaneum.
Cai Lun presents paper-making to the Han court (traditional date).
The Roman Empire reaches its greatest extent under Trajan.
Ptolemy writes the Almagest in Alexandria (c. 150).
The Mishnah is compiled under Judah ha-Nasi (c. 200).
The Han dynasty ends; China divides into the Three Kingdoms.
Ardashir I founds the Sasanian Persian Empire.
The Classic period of Maya civilisation begins in Mesoamerica (c. 250).
Chandragupta I founds the Gupta Empire in India (c. 320).
The Goths cross the Danube into the Roman Empire.
The Visigoths under Alaric sack Rome.
Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, the last emperor in the West.
The Tang dynasty begins in China.
The Hijra: Muhammad moves from Mecca to Medina, year 1 of the Islamic calendar.
Death of Muhammad; the Arab conquests begin.
The Umayyad caliphate is founded, with its capital at Damascus.
The Abbasids overthrow the Umayyads; Baghdad is founded in 762.
Vikings raid the monastery of Lindisfarne.
The House of Wisdom flourishes in Baghdad (c. 830).
The Diamond Sutra, the oldest dated printed book, is printed in China.
The Song dynasty begins in China.
Norse sailors reach North America (Vinland, c. 1000).
The Seljuk Turks defeat the Byzantines at Manzikert.
Minamoto no Yoritomo becomes shogun; warrior rule in Japan.
King John of England accepts Magna Carta.
The Mongols sack Baghdad and end the Abbasid caliphate.
Marco Polo sets out for the court of Kublai Khan.
The Ming dynasty is founded in China.
Zheng He’s fleets begin their voyages across the Indian Ocean.
Pachacuti begins the expansion of the Inca Empire (c. 1438).
Gutenberg’s printed Bible is completed in Mainz (c. 1455).
Granada falls to Castile; Columbus reaches the Caribbean.
Vasco da Gama reaches India by sea.
The Ottomans conquer Mamluk Egypt and Syria.
Tenochtitlan falls to Cortés and his allies.
Babur founds the Mughal Empire in India.
Copernicus publishes On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres.
The Tokugawa shogunate is established in Japan.
The English found Jamestown in Virginia.
Haiti becomes independent after the only successful slave revolution.
Napoleon is defeated at Waterloo; the Congress of Vienna redraws Europe.
Most of Spanish America has won independence (by 1825).
Revolutions sweep Europe; Marx and Engels publish the Communist Manifesto.
Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species.
Russia emancipates its serfs; the American Civil War begins.
The Meiji Restoration begins Japan’s modernisation.
The Berlin Conference sets rules for the colonial partition of Africa.
Revolutions in Russia; the Bolsheviks take power.
The Wall Street Crash begins the Great Depression.
Atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki; the United Nations is founded.
The People’s Republic of China is proclaimed.
Seventeen African countries become independent, the “Year of Africa”.
The attacks of 11 September in the United States.
